sources.source_name: Houston Permitting Center - Residential Plan Review
requirements: A building permit is required for most residential projects inside the corporate City of Houston limits.
New residential applicants should collect the information identified by the New Single Family Prerequisite Checklist.
New construction requires a deed restrictions declaration form.
A Wastewater Capacity Reservation letter is required before submitting plans for review.
Plans and required documents are submitted electronically through the City's permitting workflow and ProjectDox.
sources.notes: Official City of Houston residential plan review guidance. Project-specific applicability must still be validated.

sources.source_name: Houston Permitting Center - Residential Site Development Permit
requirements: Residential site development review may involve structural, planning, utilities, stormwater, traffic, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, infrastructure, forestry, sprinkler, fire, health, engineering, or floodplain review depending on project scope.
A building permit application and complete set of plans are required for residential site development review.
Architectural, structural, civil, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, sprinkler, fire alarm, or fire suppression drawings may be required depending on project scope.
sources.notes: Official City of Houston permit guidance. Discipline applicability depends on project conditions and scope.

requirements: The City permit portal supports permit applications, permit printing, permit search, payments, inspection scheduling, and permit progress tracking.
sources.notes: Official City of Houston permit portal.
